recipes.name: Fluffy Swedish Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon butter, melted, or as needed

steps.text: Blend eggs, milk, warm water, white sugar, flour, and salt together in a large mixing bowl with an electric mixer until well combined into a smooth batter.
Stream the melted butter into the batter while continuing to beat.
Heat a skillet or crepe pan over medium heat. Coat the cooking surface with a thin layer of butter.
Pour a thin layer of batter onto the prepared cooking surface; swirl the pan to assure even coverage.
Cook the crepe until browned on the bottom, 1 to 2 minutes; flip the crepe and continue cooking until the other side is browned. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Fluffy Swedish Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These sweet and fluffy crepes are a big hit in my home!

review.reviewBody: These turn out great for me. However, the second time I went to make it, I had to DROP CALORIES. I turned the milk into non-fat/skim, used 1 tbsp sugar (react to most fake sugars), took 1/4 c to 1 tbsp olive oil, and cut the egg yolk and just used egg whites (3 tbsp egg white purchased in a container equals a whole large egg). I also used multi-grain for the regular flour. FOR those of you who are stuck like me wanting yummy things but needing to alter, this dropped a lot of calories. I also added 1/2 tsp vanilla to add more flavor and sweetening. And, best of all, using these basic techniques for changing out, worked wonderfully. I have a great non-stick pan, and didn't even have to grease it. I can still have crepes -- but the recipe above, for people who aren't on a health concern -- ENJOY!! They are wonderful.

I had great success with this recipe. Best recipe I've come across for Swedish Pancakes. I altered it slightly by using brown sugar instead of white sugar and King Arthur unbleached flour. I also used a BlendTec blender to mix the ingredients. Came out Yummy!

I made this recipe for 8 adults and everyone LOVED it. We often go to IKEA for Swedish Pancakes and these are even better! I don't put butter in the pan as the butter from the batter melted in the pan and worked very well. The pancakes were golden brown and we had an assembly line going to get them done quickly. We used strawberry pie filling and fresh bananas to fill and top. Delicious. Have made a few times.

Loved it! Added teaspoon of vanilla. Served with a little bit of jelly rolled in it. And a teeny tiny bit of maple syrup, but it really wasn't necessary.

Update: we made these again and filled with a cream cheese/apricot jelly mixture. YUM! Didn't take much of the mixture. Served without syrup. Also made it on our large electric griddle - could make more at a time. Poured 1/4 cup of mixture and gently spread with back of spoon. Didn't need much spreading because the batter is so thin - really just did it to round them out a little.

I only made a couple small changes. I used about 25% of the salt, I don't care for much salt, generally. 

I separated the eggs, and beat the egg whites until soft peaks formed, like my Swedish grandmother taught me, and I browned the butter before adding it (which makes EVERYTHING better). I mixed everything together as directed except the egg whites, which I gently folded in last and let rest for 20 minutes before frying. No butter is needed in the skillet, since it's already in the batter. 

They turned out fabulous. Eggy, light and with great flavor. Just like they're supposed to be!

The person cooking these generally doesn't eat with the family, just warning you... ;) They're best served hot off the pan.

These were wonderful and made 8 very fluffy Swedish pancakes (I divided the batter evenly into 8 ramekins to make sure I was using the correct amount for each pancake). I made a few changes to make it dairy-free and a bit healthier: unsweetened almond milk in place of regular milk; 1 tbs. sugar + 3 packets of stevia in place of the 3 tbs. sugar; and 6 tbs. Smart Balance Light instead of the 1/2 cup butter. I used my nonstick crepe pan, so no extra fat was needed for greasing. I rolled up each pancake and topped them with a mixture of warmed and maple-sweetened blueberries and bananas. My husband gobbled them up and requested them again, and I definitely agreed. In fact, I think I'll be making them again this weekend! Just remember that this is *not* something you can cook quickly, as each pancake has to be done invididually. The batter comes together very quickly, the finished product . . . not so much : )

I have made this recipe a million times. I use either soy or almond milk, depending what I have on hand and they come out great! We love to fill ours with a little jam or Nutella. Just make sure to pour these VERY thin, because they do fluff up quite a bit. Also, I use 1/4 cup of butter in the batter and I don't coat the pan with butter, but use Pam instead. Works well and cuts some calories/fat.

I love how easy these are to flip. I added a teaspoon of vanilla for more flavor. for a filling we used cream cheese half-and-half sugar and vanilla to taste, blended until smooth and creamy. we served with fresh strawberries and whip cream.
Made a half recipe for me and my daughter, but separated the egg whites and beat them until slightly stiff. Folded them in at the very end. Delicious flavour!

Excellent! I liked that these were not too thick and not too thin. I halved the recipe and got five 7" pancakes. I followed the advice of some reviewers and also cut the melted butter going into the pancakes in half (worked fine) and added 1/2 tsp vanilla to this half-batch. I thought that added a nice flavor. I used these like crepes, adding a mixture of cottage cheese and a little sour cream, topped with confect sugar, a little sugar-free maple syrup and sour cream on the side. Will definitely make these again!

These were sooo good!!! I halved the recipe for two people and put butter on them sprinkled with powdered sugar and a squeez of lemon. We almost died at how good they were. We wished I had made the full recipe. I added a bit of vanilla extract and they came out tasting just like the crepes at my favorite breakfast joint. My daughter said they were better. I also love not having to wait an hour for the batter to rest like other crepe recipes.

If an omelet and a pancake had a baby, this would be the result. It's got a springy texture like egg and it's a little bread-like but certainly not bready like pancake. The texture is odd to me as it's not one or the other and I'm not sure I like it just alone with some powdered sugar. I do think this would be a fantastic base to wrap a variety of fillings from savory to sweet and it would make a great meal. The flavor on this was fine and not too sweet, not too boring, but also bland enough to work as a wrapper for anything from chicken filling and then topped with a sauce or gravy, ham and veggies with a cheese sauce, berries with whipped cream, strawberries with a chocolate glaze drizzle, the possibilities are whatever you can imagine. I didn't use a mixer. Using a whisk, I simply mixed the wet ingredients together first (except the butter) and then added that to the dry ones a little at a time, so it was easy to blend, and then once I had that homogenous, I added the butter. This was so easy and quick to put together. They cook quickly and look pretty plated up too. This is such a nice dish. I just have to get past the bouncy egg like texture. I am not a fan of eggs, and while it doesn't taste eggy, it feels eggy. I'm weird about textures. This dish is perfectly fine, it's just me.

These were SO good! I’ve been making French crepes for 20 years and this is the first time I made these Swedish pancakes. They were a bit thicker, they were fluffy, and had a great texture, flavor and consistency. My family and I prefer them now. Definitely my new go-to! Thank you!

I love this recipe. I use it for breakfast and lunch. I will make batches when my eggs or milk are about to go bad, storing the crepes in the fridge to use later for lunch packing. My bf is a very picky eater and doesn't usually let me cook for him, yet he will ask me to make these crepes and turkey bacon in the morning. he'll even run to the store for the ingredients just so I'll make them. He eats his with powdered sugar, but I've used strawberries, blackberries, homemade whipped cream, avocado, mozzarella, chicken, etc. I like to use a mini skillet to make mini crepes. These have been perfect for making bite sized snacks and breakfasts. And I add vanilla extract if i plan on using it with sugar or fruit. I highly suggest adding the warm water last, it helps with mixing better. And also letting the batter chill in the fridge so you can make thinner crepes. Low-medium heat keeps them from burning. Try lukewarm batter at a low cook temp to make crispy thin crepes chips.
We love these with sprinkled sugar and cinnamon. They have a great texture which stays moist and they cook up easier than crepes. Great recipe!
It is so good and so easy to make!
Fast, easy, simple recipe that tastes good. I will definitely make again. No more buying the boxed recipe.
Used 1/2 the butter, about 6 pt each. Made 8
To greasy, A little bit too much sugar. Great when you make whole wheat flour, and sour cream
I added a quarter of teaspoon of nutmeg to the batter very delicious. My family enjoy it.
